faq.a: Fayez is associated with the Arabic form فَايِز, whose core sense is fayez; victorious, successful.

faq.q: What is the origin of Fayez?
faq.a: Fayez is associated with Arabic. Fayez is Arabic فَائِز (Fāʾiz), the active participle of فَازَ, meaning 'victorious, successful'.
Yes — the underlying form فَايِز is Arabic.
Fayez can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Fayez should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Fāʾiz is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.a: In Urdu, Fayez is rendered فائز and carries the sense فائز، کامیاب.

faq.q: What does Fayez mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Fayez is rendered فایز and carries the sense فایز، پیروز.
A romanized syllable approximation is fayez. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Fayez?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Fayez, fayez. Script forms are فائز, فايز, فایز, فَايِز, फ़ाइज़.

faq.q: Is Fayez a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
